newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says Christopher departure shows U.S. failed.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Christopher departure shows U.S. failed.

text.p: Iran said the resignation of U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and the expected departure of Defence Secretary Willian Perry showed American policies in the Middle East had failed.

"The reshuffling of the secretaries of state and defence, in that country in the new administration, is an indication of the failure of American defence and foreign policies, particularly in this region," Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Thursday night.
"And this was predictable for us," he added in a programme on state-run television monitored by BBC radio.
U.S. President Bill Clinton accepted the resignation of Christopher on Thursday as he moved swiftly to put some fresh faces in his cabinet after his Tuesday re-election victory.

He said he had made no decision on a successor for Christopher, who worked for peace in the Middle East, Bosnia and Haiti, among other places. Perry is another big name expected to leave as Clinton prepares for his second term.
Iran has said it sees no quick change in its confrontation with the United States after Clinton's re-election.

The United States imposed a trade and investment ban on Iran in June 1995, accusing it of sponsoring terrorism and seeking to develop nuclear weapons. Iran denies the charges and says the United States is bent on destroying the Islamic government.

Washington sharpened its campaign to isolate Tehran in August this year, threatening to apply a new law which tightened the sanctions to include non-U.S. firms who invest at least $40 million in Iran's vital oil and gas industry.

It broke diplomatic ties with Tehran in 1980 after Moslem militants seized the U.S. embassy there, holding 52 Americans hostage for 444 days in the wake of the Islamic revolution that toppled the late shah, a close U.S. ally.
